extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, OED staff and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, rules, and procedural requirements the USPTO uses to assess practitioner misconduct and to impose/supervise sanctions (suspension, reinstatement conditions, probation, publication, costs). Applies to conduct before the USPTO and related client-fund/communication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction to discipline practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory/regulatory authority to bring/proceed with discipline; prerequisite for any disciplinary Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO professional rules (temporal rule split)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective May 3, 2013, the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901) apply to persons who practice before the Office; the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. § 10.xx) governs conduct prior to May 3, 2013.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When misconduct spans the May 3, 2013 date, both the pre-2013 Code and post-2013 Rules may apply to conduct occurring before and after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(a) — Disreputable or gross misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in disreputable or gross misconduct (pre-2013 Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in this matter: failing to pay government filing fees in multiple applications despite receiving funds from clients. Used as a ground for disciplinary findings for pre-May 3, 2013 conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4) — Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (pre-2013 Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner received client funds for fees but did not remit fees to USPTO (misrepresentation by omission regarding handling of client funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.23 (via (c)(8)) — Failure to inform client of significant correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to inform a client of significant correspondence from the Office that a reasonable practitioner would believe the client should be notified about (pre-2013 Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: not advising clients of Notices to File Missing Parts, Notices of Abandonment, or Final Rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.77 — Neglect
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglect of a legal matter (pre-2013 Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes failing to remit filing fees after receiving them from clients, failing to inform clients of important Office communications, and failing to respond to Office communications, resulting in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112 — Failure to deposit client funds into identifiable account
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to deposit funds paid by a client into an identifiable bank account (pre-2013 Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner lacked a client trust account and deposited client funds into an account that also contained practitioner's own funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 — Competent representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to provide competent representation by not using methods and procedures meeting the standards of competent practitioners (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: failing to pay government filing fees despite clients' advance payments; not responding to Office communications; allowing multiple applications to go abandoned; failing to timely file Petitions for Revival; failing to advise clients of Notices of Abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — Reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied for conduct such as failing to pay government filing fees, not responding to Office communications, and failing to timely file/complete required actions, causing harm to clients' matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2) — Reasonable consultation about means
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes not informing clients about important Office communications (Notices to File Missing Parts, Notices of Abandonment), options for responding, consequences of failing to respond, and failing to consult before filing Petitions for Revival.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — Keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes not advising clients of correspondence with the Office such as Notices to File Missing Parts, Notices of Abandonment, Final Rejections, Petitions to Revive, and dismissals thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4) — Respond to client's reasonable requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to respond to a client's reasonable requests for information (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied when practitioner repeatedly fails to return client communications or answer reasonable status inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(a) — Hold client property separate; keep complete records
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to hold client property in the practitioner's possession separate from the practitioner's own property and to keep complete records of such funds (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires establishment of client trust account and maintenance of financial records for funds received in connection with a representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(c) — Deposit advance fees and expenses into client trust account
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to deposit into a client trust account legal fees and expenses that have been paid in advance, to be withdrawn only as fees are earned or expenses incurred (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: practitioner did not deposit prepaid attorneys' fees and USPTO filing-fee advances into trust account and instead used/mixed funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(d) — Prompt delivery of client funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to promptly deliver to a client any funds that the client is entitled to receive (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes failure to refund filing fees or other advances that were not remitted to the Office or otherwise not earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d) — Refund of unearned advance fees on termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to refund any advance fee or expense that has not been earned or incurred by the attorney upon termination of the representation (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must return unearned advances when representation ends; failure to do so supports discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 — Unauthorized practice of law before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in the unauthorized practice of law by practicing before the Office while not an active member in good standing of a State Bar (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: practitioner continued to practice trademark law before the USPTO while administratively suspended by the State Bar of Texas.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — Conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (post-2013 Rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner failed to pay filing fees despite receiving funds, failed to reimburse clients for unperformed work, and lied to clients about status of their matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of misconduct constituting violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific practitioner behaviors that the Office treats as violations of the above rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed behaviors include: receiving client funds for USPTO fees but not remitting them; failing to deposit prepaid funds into a client trust account; not notifying clients of Notices to File Missing Parts, Notices of Abandonment, or Final Rejections; failing to respond to Office communications; filing Petitions for Revival but not paying petition fees; lying to clients about status; failing to refund unearned advances; and practicing while suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction: Suspension from practice before the Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for a specified period (here: four years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension period commences on the date the Final Order is signed; reinstatement requires satisfying listed conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement prerequisites — MPRE requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before seeking reinstatement, practitioner must take the Multi-State Professional Responsibility Examination (MPRE) and attain a score of 85 or better, providing a declaration and corroborating documents verifying compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPRE score of 85+ is required evidence of familiarity with professional responsibility prior to reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement prerequisite — Establish client trust account
rubrics_metrics.description: Before being reinstated, practitioner must submit proof that he has established a client trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office requires evidence of an appropriately established separate client trust account as a condition of reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement prerequisite — Reimbursement of clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Before reinstatement, practitioner must provide satisfactory proof that he has reimbursed all named clients in the disciplinary Complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific clients are identified; practitioner must fully reimburse fees/expenses paid in advance that were not remitted or for work not performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 and 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must comply with rules governing petitions for reinstatement (11.58) and procedures for disciplinary proceedings and costs (11.60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes following the procedural requirements and providing required documentation when seeking reinstatement and paying disciplinary costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice briefly to facilitate compliance with reinstatement requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Office may grant limited recognition to practice for a short, defined period (here: 30 days) solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly tailored and temporary; here granted so practitioner can set affairs in order before suspension commences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary monitoring and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reinstatement, practitioner shall serve a probationary period (here: two years) and during probation must submit, every six months, copies of records required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(f) and certify client trust account compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probationary reporting is at practitioner's expense and is used to monitor compliance with trust-account and record-keeping obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement during probation — Order to Show Cause and possible immediate suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED Director believes practitioner failed to comply during probation, OED Director will issue an Order to Show Cause, give practitioner 15 days to respond, and may request immediate suspension for up to one year if noncompliance persists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process: (A) Order to Show Cause sent to practitioner's last address; (B) 15 days to respond; (C) if unresolved, OED delivers record to USPTO Director requesting immediate suspension for up to one year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary actions are publicly posted; Official Gazette notice summarizes suspension, probation, reinstatement conditions, and misconduct summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall pay the costs of the disciplinary proceeding pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs are recoverable under the cited regulation and are a part of the imposed sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of disciplinary record on future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding in future complaints or proceedings as an aggravating factor, to rebut representations, or in requests for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 and related provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner's disciplinary record may be used to increase penalties in future matters or to rebut claims of rehabilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to seek reconsideration or appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may waive rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, to have the Final Order reviewed under § 11.57, or otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A waiver, when present in a settlement, forecloses typical administrative review/appeal avenues.
